outcomes.question: Before I put time into this: is it well regarded? Has it been criticised or superseded?
outcomes.text:
It's worth your time, and it's been contested. It won the 2025 Berggruen essay prize [spya-gp3g6s]. I found no sign that it's been superseded. There are published replies, including [Armando Vieira's Medium reply](https://medium.com/@Lidinwise/why-the-mythology-of-conscious-ai-misses-the-deeper-point-437589461d45). He accepts Seth's case against computational functionalism but says biology alone doesn't explain experience. [Ethics in Review](https://www.ethicsinreview.com/on-anil-seths-the-mythology-of-conscious-ai-part-1/) has another reply. These would give your group something to argue about.

Do you want to lead the discussion or just take part?

outcomes.question: What should I read before or alongside this to get the most out of it?
outcomes.text:
You don't need anything before it; the essay is self-contained. For a discussion, read it first, then one reply. Barton Friedland's [What The AI Consciousness Question Conceals](https://www.downes.ca/post/79047) (Stephen Downes's summary, linked) answers Seth directly. You could also read [a blog response](https://www.ethicsinreview.com/on-anil-seths-the-mythology-of-conscious-ai-part-1/).

Do you want the group to argue about the claim itself or its ethical conclusions?

outcomes.question: Who is the author, and how far should I trust them on this subject?
outcomes.text:
Seth is a neuroscientist at Sussex and director of its Centre for Consciousness Science [spya-rg493b]. That makes him a credible voice, but not a neutral one. His "controlled hallucination" account of perception is the base of the essay's life-matters argument [spya-xhvztm]. Reviewers of his work say it [sidesteps the hard problem](https://mountainsrivers.com/2022/12/04/the-real-problem-of-consciousness-a-review-of-being-you-by-anil-seth/) and [offers little guidance on AI](https://www.cell.com/current-biology/pdf/S0960-9822(22)01017-X.pdf). He also calls his own view a minority one [spya-qu7j89].

Should your group's discussion focus on his argument or on the ethics?

outcomes.question: I found this page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_naturalism Is it worth reading alongside this piece?
outcomes.text:
Yes, as a short companion. [The Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_naturalism) covers Searle's original version, which is narrower than Seth's. It says Searle doesn't rule out artificial consciousness, and it lists critics such as Fodor and Haugeland. Seth calls his own position a variant and admits it's a minority view [spya-qu7j89]. Read the page after the essay, as background.

Which would help your group more: the essay's whole argument, or just its section on life mattering [spya-hj5y6s]?

outcomes.text:
It's widely read and contested, and Gwern has already followed it up himself. His [Scaling Hypothesis Revisited](https://gwern.net/scaling-hypothesis-revisited) is a 2022 sequel, and the piece points to it [spya-ewxv9q]. One outside critique is [Is the Scaling Hypothesis Falsifiable?](https://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/23622/1/psa_scaling_hypothesis_manuscript.pdf). It's worth your time, and the closing critics section is where a group will argue [spya-zyncdd].

outcomes.question: What should I read before or alongside this to get the most out of it?
outcomes.text:
For a counterweight, [Gary Marcus's skeptical piece](https://garymarcus.substack.com/p/does-ai-really-need-a-paradigm-shift) pairs well, and so does Gwern's [two-years-later followup](https://gwern.net/scaling-hypothesis-revisited). The two papers the argument leans on are [Kaplan et al.'s scaling laws](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361) [spya-sctj6d] and the [GPT-3 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165) [spya-vn0xpd]. Skim both for the graphs.

outcomes.question: Who is the author, and how far should I trust them on this subject?
outcomes.text:
Gwern is an independent writer. By [his own account](https://gwern.net/me) he has no formal academic post, and [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=yk1QMowAAAAJ) lists him as independent. The piece is an advocate's argument, so weigh his forecasts against his rhetoric, such as the "voice of authority" passage [spya-zyncdd]. He also admits his earlier doubt [spya-emqjaa]. One later paper asks whether the [scaling hypothesis is falsifiable](https://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/23622/1/psa_scaling_hypothesis_manuscript.pdf).
